READ-ONLY diagnosis of the Nxeon migration engine at /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (~6600 lines). Do NOT modify any files. Return a root cause with exact file:line anchors and a concrete minimal fix.

## Problem
When the engine brings up multiple Docker Compose projects on the target, `/opt/mailserver` fails with:
`network soulpilates_internal declared as external, but could not be found`

This is a cross-project network dependency: mailserver's compose references an EXTERNAL network (`soulpilates_internal`) that ANOTHER migrated compose project (soulpilates) defines/creates. Because the projects are brought up in an arbitrary order (and a project that declares a network `external: true` will NOT create it), mailserver comes up before the network exists, or the network is namespaced under a different compose project name.

## Investigate (cite file:line)
1. The compose bring-up loop — search `composeDirs`, `Bringing up`, `compose up`, `Compose up`, `composeCmd`, `composeFileArg`, `composeEnvFor`. It is around line 5354-5410 (may have shifted). How are the projects ORDERED? (Probably input/scan order — arbitrary.)
2. Whether the engine ever pre-creates external networks. Search `docker network create`, `network inspect`, `networks`.
3. How compose picks the project name / whether COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME is set — this decides the actual network name (`<project>_<net>`). A network declared `external: true` in mailserver as `soulpilates_internal` must match a network literally named `soulpilates_internal` — so the DEFINING project must create it under that exact name (compose only auto-prefixes non-external networks).
4. Read the failing run's stored record for how compose projects/networks look: from /opt/nxeon run `node -e 'const {PrismaClient}=require("@prisma/client");const p=new PrismaClient();p.migration.findUnique({where:{id:"cmsciv67q0005hlhwo5vzzu7h"},select:{items:true,log:true}}).then(r=>{console.log((r.log||"").split("\n").filter(l=>/network|compose|Compose|Bringing/i.test(l)).join("\n"));console.log("COMPOSE DIRS:",JSON.stringify((r.items&&r.items.composeDirs)||(r.items&&r.items.scan&&r.items.scan.appDirs)))})'`

## Deliverable
Concrete minimal fix: e.g. (a) before the bring-up loop, scan each project's compose file(s) for `networks:` with `external: true` and pre-create any that are missing with `docker network create <name>` (idempotent), and/or (b) order the bring-up so projects that DEFINE a referenced network come up first (topological by external-network references). Preserve the honest missing-secrets gate. Give exact insertion points (file:line) and the shell/TS to add. Note whether reading the compose file's networks requires a small remote `docker compose config` call or a YAML grep on the target. Be concrete.
